Let the coloring have \(m\) red runs and \(m\) blue runs (if both colors appear).  
Let \(t\) be the number of red runs of length \(1\), and \(u\) the number of blue runs of length \(1\).

- Adjacent red faults: a red run of length \(a\) contributes \(a-1\), so total \(= r-m\), where \(r\) is the number of red dots.
- Blue pairs exactly two apart: a blue run of length \(b\) contributes \(\max(0,b-2)\) internal such pairs, and each red run of length \(1\) creates one cross blue pair. Thus blue faults \(=\sum \max(0,b_i-2)+t = b-2m+u+t\).

So total faults:
\[
F=(r-m)+(b-2m+u+t)=1000-3m+u+t.
\]

Now let \(q=u+t\). Since the non-length-1 runs have length at least \(2\),
\[
1000 \ge 4m-q \quad\Rightarrow\quad q\ge 4m-1000.
\]
Thus
\[
3m-q \le 
\begin{cases}
3m \le 750, & m\le 250,\\
1000-m \le 750, & m\ge 250.
\end{cases}
\]
Therefore
\[
F=1000-(3m-q)\ge 1000-750=250.
\]

Equality occurs when \(m=250\) and \(u=t=0\), i.e. all runs have length exactly \(2\): pattern \(RRBB\) repeated \(250\) times. Then the only faults are the \(250\) adjacent red pairs.

\[
\boxed{250}
\]
